title: Order contract decision lab
description: Select a client intent to trace the resource, method, and ownership path it needs. The contract result explains the promise a client can rely on.

nodes.label: Client
nodes.detail: Sends an authenticated request with a method, target, headers, and optional representation. The client should be able to decide whether and how to retry from the documented contract.

nodes.label: API boundary
nodes.detail: Authenticates the caller, enforces authorization and limits, validates the representation, and attaches a request ID before the request reaches domain logic.

nodes.label: Orders collection
nodes.detail: Represents many orders. A GET reads a filtered, bounded collection; a POST accepts a new-order representation and may create a new order resource.

nodes.label: Order resource
nodes.detail: Represents one identified order. It is the target for a safe read and a stable reference in related resources such as cancellation records.

nodes.label: Cancellations
nodes.detail: Represents cancellation records with a reason, timestamp, actor, and policy result. It preserves order history instead of treating cancellation as deletion.

nodes.label: Order service
nodes.detail: Applies ownership, inventory, cancellation-policy, and idempotency rules. HTTP routing should not decide whether an order may be cancelled.

nodes.label: Order store
nodes.detail: Stores order and cancellation facts, including the records needed to return a consistent outcome after a retried write.

scenarios.label: List orders
scenarios.summary: The client needs a bounded, filtered page of many orders. It reads the collection with GET and receives a deterministic continuation token when another page exists.
scenarios.result: Use GET /v1/orders with documented filters, limit, cursor, and ordering. The collection is read-only here, so a retry must not create or mutate an order.

scenarios.label: Create once
scenarios.summary: The client submits a new order representation. The collection routes the request to the order service, which validates the request and writes the authoritative order exactly once for the supplied idempotency key.
scenarios.result: Use POST /v1/orders with an Idempotency-Key. The resource path names the collection; the service owns new IDs, validation, and the replay-safe result.

scenarios.label: Record cancellation
scenarios.summary: The client records a cancellation against a known order. The cancellation resource reaches the order service, where state and policy determine whether the order can transition.
scenarios.result: Use POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/cancellations when cancellation needs an audit trail or separate lifecycle. DELETE would make a meaningful historical fact disappear.
